cache_lifecycle_reconstructed.before: ossl_x509v3_cache_extensions wrote each cache slot into the X509 at the point of decode (crldp, skid, akid, altname, nc, rfc3779_addr, rfc3779_asid), and wrote ex_pathlen/ex_kusage/ex_xkusage/ex_nscert/sha1_hash/ex_flags incrementally. A lock-free reader could observe a half-built cache, and setup_crldp installed the decoded stack before validating its points.
cache_lifecycle_reconstructed.after: CacheBuild::build decodes and derives every output into local owned state and touches no cache member of X509. Each decoded value is owned by CacheValue<T> (NonNull + the authority's release) or is None on a failed decode. CacheBuild::publish installs all seven slots and all scalars in one place while the write lock is held; ossl_x509_init_sig_info runs next; the final ex_flags store (flags | EXFLAG_SET) is the single publication point. A certificate whose extensions are invalid is published as the authority's complete invalid state (successfully decoded slots + EXFLAG_INVALID), because x509_vfy consumes those slots even when the cache call returns 0 — 'no partially installed state' means no partially built slot and no pre-publication cache write, not zero installed slots.
cache_lifecycle_reconstructed.teardown: ossl_x509v3_cache_free re-adopts each installed slot with the same CacheValue owner, releases it, and clears the slot. It is called by X509's ASN1_OP_D2I_PRE and ASN1_OP_FREE_POST arms, replacing the previous partial skid-only release. A second call is a no-op.
cache_lifecycle_reconstructed.owner_count: one owner per slot: the staging CacheValue is consumed by publish (into_raw) or by the teardown re-adoption; no value has two live owners

sync_unsafecell_contract.guaranteed_by_types: XstandardTable is #[repr(transparent)] over UnsafeCell<[X509Purpose; 10]>, and its unsafe impl Sync makes XSTANDARD usable as a static and permits X509_PURPOSE_add to rewrite a reserved row in place. XPTABLE is an AtomicPtr<OpenSslStack>, so the stack pointer slot itself is race-free.
sync_unsafecell_contract.not_guaranteed_by_types: Neither type enforces single-threaded use. AtomicPtr orders pointer publication only; it does not make the stack elements or a reserved row safe to mutate concurrently. The accessors hand out *mut rows, so a caller can hold a raw borrow while another thread rewrites or frees the table. The Sync claim is therefore conditional on the authority's unlocked, single-threaded purpose-table discipline, now stated explicitly on XstandardTable, XPTABLE and X509_PURPOSE_add's # Safety section.
sync_unsafecell_contract.enforcement_choice: not enforced with a lock: the authority takes none, adding one would serialise callbacks and cannot be dropped into the C ABI without a behavioural change; the obligation is recorded as an explicit caller obligation

lock_coverage_findings.writes: every cache-slot write now happens inside ossl_x509v3_cache_extensions under CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock, except the single publication store of ex_flags. X509_set_proxy_flag locks; X509_set_proxy_pathlen writes ex_pcpathlen with no lock (authority behaviour, pre-existing).
lock_coverage_findings.covered_reads: all public cache accessors (X509_get_extension_flags/key_usage/extended_key_usage/get0_* identifiers/path lengths, X509_get_signature_info) call X509_check_purpose first, which takes the write lock; the lock acquire/release gives them a happens-before view of the completed cache.
lock_coverage_findings.uncovered_reads: x509_vfy deliberately reads crldp, nc, altname, akid, skid and ex_flags without a lock (crl_crldp_check, check_name_constraints, check_id). This is safe only when the cache was completed before the certificate was shared, or when the same thread completed it (check_extensions/X509_check_purpose runs before those readers). No lock was added, matching the authority; cross-thread safety of a lock-free read that races the first build is NOT established.
lock_coverage_findings.crldp_name: crldp_full_name builds a fresh X509_NAME on demand and never stores it in the published distribution point, so the one post-publication write that would have raced readers (dpname) is absent.
lock_coverage_findings.verified: lock acquisition and publication order read back from the final source; no runtime race detector was run

crldp_mitigation_confirmation.mechanism: setup_crldp no longer expands relative names; setup_dp validates reason flags only; crldp_full_name (x509_vfy.c 3.6.5 shape) builds the derived name on demand and the caller frees it
crldp_mitigation_confirmation.measurement: 64 relative DPs x 4818 B expanded issuer name = 308352 B (eager cost that was avoided); every dpname is NULL after ossl_x509v3_cache_extensions
crldp_mitigation_confirmation.compat_note: setup_crldp can no longer return -1; it returns a Decoded value whose valid=false on a malformed/invalid point, matching the 3.6.5 divergence already recorded in cve-crldp-2026-35189.json
